notes.title: v0.2.56+83 *FUSION REACTOR*
notes.notes:
[list]
[*] Major addition to the game's audio system - it is now possible to have environmental loops (see below).
[*] Player can now hear fire.
[*] Player can now hear nature sounds (water lapping on the shore, forest sounds).
[*] Wading through water now sounds different from normal steps.
[*] When enemies (the Order) get sufficiently annoyed, the music changes.
[*] Some changes to sounds and volume.
[*] New in-game console command: "loadout problems" lists current problems with the player's robot loadout. Also, the existing "award" console command is now "loadout award".
[*] It is now impossible to start a sector with an invalid loadout. The "LOADOUT" button is highlighted in that case.
[*] The loadout screen highlights subsystems that have been depleted and cannot be used.
[*] Reward the player with a subsystem right after the tutorial (so they don't need to wait until level 3 to have their first decision).
[*] Workaround for a bug in the UI engine -- it is currently NOT possible to change the volume of anything in the settings. This is because of a bug in "slider". Will reinstate once that bug is addressed.
[*] Subtly more cinematic loading screen
[/list]

notes.title: v0.2.51+78 *ALPHONSE*
notes.notes:
[list]
[*] Hardpoints are now external and internal, and there's now more space for internal subsystems
[*] Subsystems now have versions (e.g. Autocannon M1)
[*] When in loadout, it's now possible to compare two subsystems at a glance
[*] Added another map (will randomly rotate with the one you already know)
[*] Standardize UI (e.g. screen name at top left, back button at bottom left, help at bottom right, etc.)
[*] More things on the screen now react to mouse-over and show help
[*] Improved human rewards UI
[*] Humans now sometimes let you choose between two subsystems
[*] Add new sounds
[*] Added ability for some smoke grenades to make more smoke (and, generally speaking, for weapons having differing effects)
[*] Add a subsystems database that helps keep subsystem definitions in one place (useful for rewards and, in the future, modding)
[*] Add 'award' console command
[*] Animate the loading screen a bit more so that it's easier to detect jank
[*] Fix long-standing bug in map offset serialization (only relevant for modding)
[*] 
[/list]

notes.title: v0.2.50+77 *ZENTRAEDI*
notes.notes:
[list]
[*] New sounds
[*] Stability improvements (e.g. guard against production errors)
[*] Update weapons UI slightly (no longer shows outdated key bindings)
[*] Sync key bindings help with actual key bindings
[*] Avoid trying to compute traversed tiles from outside the map

notes.title: v0.2.49+76 *YUKINAGA*
notes.notes:
[list]
[*] Subsystems (like weapons) can now have limited uses. This means you can get an overpowered machine gun, but you can only use it in, say, three sectors before you have to "give it back". This lets me give you some sweet abilities and fun weapons while keeping the game interesting.
[*] Rewards after sector are now implemented using drop tables. This also makes them less bountiful than before, which should make for more interesting runs in the future.
[*] Keyboard bindings are now re-assignable and saved with settings.
[*] List changes to resources in debrief screen (instead of the vague "ammo change")
[*] Use physical keys, not logical ones. That means that the key binding you press does not depend on your selected (localized) keyboard layout. This is what most people want from their games (i.e. you don't need to make sure you're on English layout when starting the game).
[*] Deal with URL launch failures (at least gives you a URL to copy paste).
[*] Log more useful debugging information when steam initialization fails.
[/list]

notes.title: v0.2.43+70 *SHINOHARA*

notes.title: v0.2.31+58 *GUNDAM*
notes.notes:
[list]
[*] Enemies no longer "accidentally" hit (this was realistic but unfun -- it was possible for a random enemy to take the first potshot at you and, by random chance, hit you right where it hurt you most). Instead, all entities now have "stormtrooper mode", in which their inaccurate shots are way less likely to hit. Once their aim's precision improves, all bets are off, of course. But by that time, the player has had the chance to react.
[*] UI now shows red overlay when the player's robot's structural integrity is low. This prevents "surprising" deaths.
[*] Add timestamps to console (helps with debugging - how quickly did event happen?)
[/list]

notes.title: v0.2.26+53 *BEAM SABER*
notes.notes:
Thanks everyone for playtesting. This is just a bug fix update, plus some ground work.

[list]
[*] Slightly more robust Steam integration.
[*] Fix bug that tried to show ammo count for a weapon that was just jettisoned.
[*] Add logging for important game events, for path-finding, and for menu interactions (which will let me understand what was going on when the game crashed).
[*] Fix bug which tried to start music before the audio engine was loaded.
[*] Fix minor bug when player leaves a sector before it's fully loaded (+ prevent similar bugs from appearing).
[*] Fix bug that gave player a repair pod "for free" after each level.
[/list]

notes.title: v0.2.24+51 *ZENTRAEDI*
notes.notes:
[list]
[*] Major overhaul of the loadout system. The change isn't that visible yet for the player, but it allows for basically anything to be attached to any hardpoint. This will be a major part of the strategy.
[*] Instead of missiles and shells and grenades to define themselves, I'm switching to a more understandable and simpler system. Missiles, for examples, are resources (like in the game FTL), and it depends on the used missile launcher what they'll materialize as. So you don't need to manage five different incompatible types of missiles. Instead, you switch to a newer missile pod, and all your missiles automatically work with it. This slight decrease in realism makes juggling the loadout much simpler and, frankly, way more fun.
[*] You can now bring up your loadout from within a sector. Press I.
[*] You can drag & drop subsystems in loadout screen.
[*] Fix bug with negative (fractional) damage.
[*] Placing blueprints (e.g. placing turrets and landmines) now uses the same machinery as launching missiles and such. This makes it possible, for example, to assign a button to it. I'm also pretty sure this fixed some subtle bugs in the process.
[*] The action bar is no longer hard-coded. While it's still not possible to customize it, it will intelligently enable buttons depending on installed subsystems. For example, adding a frag grenade launcher to your loadout will enable the S key for launching those.
[*] Fixed bug which let you try and use repair swarms from context menu even when you didn't have any left.
[*] You now need a functioning Repair Pod for repairs.
[*] Prevent a potential bug with waypoints "moving" after a path has been found.
[*] Fix bug in which pathfinding failed silently if you tried to move to an occupied position (but you don't see the entity occupying it). Now, pathfinding will happily find paths that are actually blocked (but the moving entity doesn't know it yet).
[/list]

notes.title: v0.2.23+50 *YUKINAGA*
notes.notes:
Just hotfixing stuff so that the playtest is less annoying.

[list]
[*] My custom screen recording binding was clashing with the normal Steam screenshot binding (F12). And it's meant for use in trailers anyway, so I got rid of it. If you've seen the game go to very low FPS, it might have been that the game was trying (and failing) to record every frame of the screen at 2x resolution...
[*] Downgrade some warnings so that the developer console doesn't show up for things that can be ignored by the player. The warnings will still be reported to me. Btw, if you want to see the console anyway, just press / (forward slash).
[*] Add more details to some of the reported warnings.
[/list]

notes.title: Playtest now available
notes.notes:
Hey there,

The playtest is now available: you only have to go the the game's page and request access.

I need to lower y'all's expectations, though. It's really an alpha / playtest, not a demo nor any kind of early access or whatever. The game is missing 99% of content (but the basic game loop and simulation systems are there). Also, it's missing table-stakes features like volume control or custom key binding support. Oh well.

I'm really looking forward to feedback, suggestions, etc!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45193969/725c8b6a992675a46264f04b5665d457b12e8be7.jpg[/img]
